scope: Esther 1–10: all 167 verses and all Notes/Vocabulary read continuously; new 7–10 source reread documented separately.
observations: Names, kinship, and adoption remain consistent. Bigthan/Bigthana follows the source distinction noted in 6:2. Haman’s ten sons are fully present in 9:7–9, including Aridatha omitted by TSW.
The irrevocable first decree and the lethal second decree retain their separate force. The children-and-women ambiguity in 8:11 is noted; 9:5 retains the victors’ discretion.
Third-year banquet, seventh-year appointment, twelfth-year lot, Nisan decree, Sivan counter-decree, and thirteenth-through-fifteenth Adar sequence remain distinct.
The repeated petition/request offers connect 5:6, 7:2–3 and 9:12. Banquets, honor, covered heads/faces, the fifty-cubit stake, and reversals retain their narrative connections.
The three refusals to take plunder are preserved despite permission in 8:11. Haman’s sons are dead before the request to display their bodies.

Mordecai’s uncertain appeal to another place, Esther’s acknowledged risk, and the lack of explicit divine naming in the Hebrew remain intact. Pur/Purim and gifts to the poor connect the ending to the threatened date.
The imperial tribute and Mordecai’s standing remain in chapter 10; the ending is not rewritten as a universal statement of approval.
limitations: This is the drafting agent’s continuous reading and focused consistency review, not independent scholarly or human editorial approval.
No earlier chapter wording or ledger was changed. Future editorial changes must rebind affected ledgers.
Companion quotations and bindings have not been installed or reconciled.
